transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Asha (Cobalt Head of ML), Liam (Platform), Sofia (Security), Tom (Product)

Summary: quick discovery focused on model selection for Cobalt's logistics assistant. Discussed context length needs (tracking docs, manifests), multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), tool-calling (manifest lookups, shipment-tracking API), and deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC). Agreed POC with 2-week benchmark across 3 models; Redwood to send pricing and security pack.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll keep this to 30-ish minutes, we're mostly doing discovery to understand model needs and deployment preferences. Maya, Diego are here to help on the technical side.
[00:08] Asha Patel: Great thanks. Quick context: we run an internal assistant for ops teams, it ingests manifests, chat history, and sometimes entire bill-of-lading PDF extracts. Need long context for a single session, often 20–40 pages, and multilingual support for EN and ES primarily, occasional FR. Latency matters for interactive use — sub 700 ms preferred but we can trade for cost on lower tiers.
[00:32] Maya Singh: Got it. When you say 20–40 pages, do you have a tokens estimate? That helps model selection — 16k context might be okay, 32k safer.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: We ran some rough counts — about 6k–10k tokens per session on average, peak up to ~25k for full manifest + conversation.
[00:48] Diego Ramos: OK that maps to 16k comfortable, 32k for peaks. For model choices, are you looking exclusively at open models or considering hosted proprietary ones?
[00:58] Asha Patel: Prefer open models for licensing and cost; want Redwood's model catalog recommendations. Also need tool-calling — we have shipment-tracking microservices that the assistant should call for real-time status, and we want structured outputs for downstream systems.
[01:12] Jordan Park: Perfect — typical tradeoff: larger open models (e.g., Llama-3 variants, Mistral 7B/22B, Mistral-Instructs, etc.) give different cost/latency/accuracy curves. For multilingual and tool-calling, we recommend a test matrix: a high-capacity 32k context model, a mid 16k model, and a smaller low-latency variant for high-frequency ops. We'll include Redwood-verified perf profiles in the POC.
[01:30] Tom Becker: How does tool-calling work with Redwood? We need function-calling style integration and also audit logs for each call.
[01:37] Maya Singh: We support structured tool-calls (function-calling) and streaming responses; our runtime can emit function triggers that your microservice can accept and return structured JSON. All calls can be logged to audit trails, and in private/VPC deployments logs can be sent to your SIEM.
[01:52] Sofia Morales: From security side: SOC2 is required, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, KMS for encryption-at-rest, and need to confirm data residency — can you support EU region only? Also how do you handle KV/prefix caching for PII?
[02:08] Diego Ramos: Yes — SOC2 and SSO are standard on our Dedicated/Private tiers; hosted customers can get SOC2 attestation and we offer SAML. For KMS, we integrate with AWS KMS and customer-managed CMKs in Dedicated and Private. For EU-only residency we have dedicated regions and can route requests there; we'll include region routing policy in the docs. Regarding cache, prefix/KV cache is opt-in; for PII you can disable cache for specific routes or encrypt cached blobs with your CMK.
[02:33] Asha Patel: Good. For model comparsion, we need to see accuracy on domain prompts — shipping terms, unimodal PDF extracts, tables. Also the assistant must output canonical JSON for our ingestion.
[02:44] Maya Singh: We'll run three model variants: 1) 32k-context open model (eg. Llama-3-32k-ish variant), 2) 16k Mistral or similar mid model, 3) optimized low-latency quantized variant on dedicated nodes. We'll test: latency, token cost, hallucination on tabular data, and function-calling reliability.
[03:02] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated vs Hosted, what's the typical throughput and scaling? We expect spikes around batch imports — tens of concurrent sessions.
[03:10] Jordan Park: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and burst policies; you can configure autoscaling. For your concurrency (tens of concurrent sessions), Dedicated should be predictable; Hosted can also handle it but may vary by tenant load. We'll propose both options in the pricing.
[03:24] Tom Becker: What about quantization and cost savings — do you support int8 or 4-bit to lower cost but keep accuracy?
[03:31] Diego Ramos: Yes — our runtime supports quantized execution paths and we provide quantization profiles. For some models we see 2–4x cost reductions with minimal accuracy impact, but results vary by model and prompt. We'll include profilings.
[03:44] Asha Patel: How do you handle model rollouts and fallback? If the 32k variant is down or overloaded, can we fall back to a 16k model gracefully? We need to preserve continuity.
[03:54] Maya Singh: You can configure routing policies: prefer low-latency region, fallback to cheaper model variant, or degrade functionality (e.g., switch to truncated context mode). We have automatic fallback to compatible variants and can flag truncated responses so your frontend can surface a warning.
[04:10] Sofia Morales: Logging and access — we need fine-grained RBAC and per-route audit logs for compliance. Also retention windows for logs: 90 days default but we may want longer in Private.
[04:20] Jordan Park: RBAC is configurable in Dedicated and Private; audit logs retention is tunable as an add-on. We'll include options in the security pack.
[04:27] Asha Patel: For the POC, timeline and success metrics — we want: 1) latency under 700 ms for interactive flows on the mid/low model, 2) hallucination rate below X on our eval set (we'll provide), 3) reliable function-calls 99% success in test runs, and 4) cost per 1k tokens under target TBD.
[04:42] Maya Singh: Sounds reasonable. For the POC we'll need a sample dataset and expected outputs to run automated evals. Also to validate multilingual we'll include prompts in EN/ES/FR and measure accuracy.
[04:56] Liam O'Connor: Integration: we use Kubernetes and Istio in our platform, will Redwood's Private option run on-prem or VPC? How does networking work?
[05:05] Diego Ramos: Private offers both customer VPC and optionally on-prem package. For VPC we provide a control plane with customer-managed networking and private endpoints; for on-prem we'll share deployment manifests for a supported infra profile. We'll document required egress rules for telemetry and any control-plane callbacks.
[05:22] Tom Becker: Any special PCI or HIPAA notes? We process PII but not PHI; still need to ensure encryption and contracts.
[05:29] Sofia Morales: HIPAA not required, but we need DPA and data processing addendum.
[05:33] Jordan Park: We'll include DPA language and can discuss custom contracts during procurement.
[05:37] Asha Patel: In terms of API surface, how do you handle streaming and partial responses? We rely on partial structured outputs to update UI while the model finishes longer parts.
[05:45] Maya Singh: Streaming supported for both text and function-calls; KV caching allows us to reuse prefixes and reduce token use while keeping latency low. You can stream partial JSON objects as they're produced.
[05:55] Liam O'Connor: Any gotchas about token counting and embeddings? We use embeddings for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — need consistent embedding dims and indexing options.
[06:03] Diego Ramos: We support embeddings via the Redwood API; you can pick dimension/profile for the model. For RAG, we recommend separate embedding index aligned with your retrieval library; we can export vectors and integrate with common vector DBs.
[06:14] Tom Becker: For the POC we want to test end-to-end: doc ingestion -> retrieval -> model generation -> function call to shipment API.
[06:20] Jordan Park: Good scope. Suggested POC steps: 1) you provide dataset subset and goals, 2) Redwood spins up sandbox capacity (hosted or dedicated) and runs benchmarks on 3 models, 3) share result dashboard and recommended config (batching, quantization, routing).
[06:33] Asha Patel: What do you need from us to start?
[06:36] Maya Singh: Sample request logs or a 1–2k sample of typical sessions, some examples of desired structured JSON outputs, and any compliance constraints (KMS type, EU residency). Also indicate preferred deployment mode for the POC (hosted sandbox vs dedicated trial).
[06:50] Asha Patel: We'll provide sample sessions and prefer hosted sandbox first to iterate quickly, then dedicated pilot if results are promising.
[06:58] Jordan Park: Great. On pricing, we'll send a comparison: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved commit, and private licensing. We'll outline cost per token, estimated monthly run-rate for your profile, and expected savings with quantization.
[07:11] Tom Becker: Can you also include expected latency numbers for each model on both hosted and dedicated? Even ballpark is fine.
[07:17] Diego Ramos: Yes — Redwood-verified perf numbers for each model and hardware profile. We'll include median p95 latency and throughput.
[07:24] Sofia Morales: For security docs, please send SOC2 report, DPA, SAML guides, and KMS integration notes. Also include audit log export formats.
[07:33] Jordan Park: Will do. We'll bundle the docs and pricing in one email and upload the POC checklist to the drive link.
[07:40] Asha Patel: One more question — tool-calling reliability under high load: if the model emits multiple function-calls in a single response, can you guarantee ordering and idempotency hints?
[07:49] Maya Singh: The runtime preserves sequence and we'll include call metadata (request id, sequence index). Idempotency is on the client side, but we'll surface the recommended patterns and headers for safe retries.
[07:59] Liam O'Connor: Any pre-built connectors for shipment-tracking providers?
[08:03] Diego Ramos: We have templates and example adapters for common REST/gRPC services; we'll share a sample adapter you can drop into your service.
[08:11] Tom Becker: Perfect. Next step: deep dive with infra next Tuesday to discuss VPC/networking details and certificate exchange if we go private.
[08:19] Jordan Park: I'll schedule that. Thanks everyone for the time — quick recap in chat and I'll follow up with pricing + security pack + POC checklist.
[08:28] Asha Patel: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
